title: 2D Spatial Reasoning with Adaptive Neural Cellular Automata
claim: Simple local update rules applied repeatedly over time can produce complex global patterns from a trivial initial state.
layout: 2 panels, top-to-bottom; large space-time grid above, rule table below
description: The figure has two stacked panels. Panel a) is a large grid in grayscale, with a space axis running left to right along the top and a time axis running downward on the left. A single gray cell at the top row grows into a triangular, fractal-like pattern of black, gray and white cells, and the pattern gets more intricate toward the bottom. The eye goes to this triangle first. Panel b) is a compact strip of seven rule boxes. Each box shows a neighborhood sum as a shaded bar, with the resulting cell state as a small square below it. Output digits 1, 0, 0, 1, 2, 1, 0 sit under the boxes. Math labels include s_{i,t}, ΣN(s_{i,t}), s_{i,t+1} := R[ΣN(s_{i,t})] and R. Blue arrows mark the axes and the update direction. Color is blue arrows plus black, white and gray.
caption: Sketch of a basic 1D Cellular Automaton with three discrete states $s_i \in \{0,1,2\}$ and seven update rules $\mathcal{R}$, which operate on the sum over a 3-cell neighborhood $\mathcal{N}$. a) shows the inference of complex patterns from an initial state by the rules visualized in b) over time.
abstract: Many modern learning approaches are still struggling with spatial reasoning tasks, i.e. they lack the ability to utilize geometric information of perceived entities and their spatial relation to each other to solve problems. We introduce a novel Adaptive Neural Cellular Automata (aNCA) architecture which uses deformable convolutions to dynamically adapt the perceptive field and iteratively reason over 2D spatial relations on grid-like data structures (e.g. images). Empirical results on public benchmarks show state of the art comprehensible results with high generalization abilities for solving image based puzzles like Sudoku or finding the shortest path in a maze.
